idea-plugin.name: Rust Portable
idea-plugin.description:
Write & run Rust in IntelliJ IDEA Community — for free. Rust Portable adds lightweight Rust support to the free IDE, with no RustRover license and no system-wide Rust install required. IntelliJ IDEA Community doesn't bundle the official Rust plugin (that's Ultimate / RustRover / CLion only), so this fills the gap.

  • Portable Rust toolchain — download a toolchain from inside the IDE (like the JDK downloader) using the official rustup. Stored under ~/.rust-portable with its own RUSTUP_HOME and CARGO_HOME, so nothing touches your shell profile or an existing system Rust. Pick stable, beta, nightly or a pinned release, and switch anytime.
  • Run with one click — a green ▶ gutter marker on fn main(), plus right-click ▸ Run. Inside a Cargo project it runs cargo run from the crate root, so relative paths resolve just like they do in a terminal. A loose .rs file with no Cargo.toml is compiled with rustc and executed, so scratch files stay runnable.
  • Code intelligence (optional) — completion, go-to-definition, hover docs and error highlighting via rust-analyzer, the same language server RustRover runs underneath, bridged with the free LSP4IJ plugin. One click adds it to your portable toolchain as an official rustup component. Fully offline; no Node.js.
  • Syntax highlighting — for .rs files (keywords, strings including raw and byte literals, lifetimes, attributes, macros, doc comments), even without the language server.
  • Run cargo tools — build / check / test / add / fmt / clippy in a console.

Active on IDEs without built-in Rust (IDEA Community, PyCharm Community, WebStorm, …). On RustRover / IDEA Ultimate / CLion the native Rust support is used instead — this plugin steps aside.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0
  • Initial release.
  • Download a portable Rust toolchain from inside the IDE via rustup (stable / beta / nightly / pinned), isolated under ~/.rust-portable.
  • Run a .rs file: ▶ gutter marker on fn main(), cargo run from the crate root, or a rustc compile-and-run for a standalone file.
  • Optional rust-analyzer code intelligence via LSP4IJ (one-click setup), lexer-based syntax highlighting, and a cargo build/check/test/add/fmt/clippy runner.
